text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Deputy Finance Minister David Magen to quit government.
- U.S. spy Jonathan Pollard to Israel's High Court: Force prime minister to acknowledge me.
- Israel beat Cyprus, 2-0.
- Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu: Peace process alive.
- Treasury: Nixing property tax to cost state revenue 150 million shekels.
- Africa Israel general manager Avigdor Kaplan may quit over differences with controlling shareholder Lev Leviev.
- Differences among committee members obstruct El Al Israel Airlines privatisation.
- Insurance available to protect against buying stolen car.
GLOBES
- Bank of Israel: Freeze of economic activity during the last six months.
HAARETZ
- High Court of Justice to hear five petitions on Bar-On affair on May 11.
- Government tried to prevent publication of Pollard's court appeal hours after its broadcast on radio.
- Israel's Solel Boneh to put shares on Tel Aviv stock exchange this month.
MAARIV
- Five High Court judges to decide on challenges to attorney-general report.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- United States: Syria continues to back terrorist organisations.
